plain: Mastercard's rules and integration paths for merchants accepting agent payments, introduced on 2025-10-14 and shared on Mastercard Developers for feedback. Mastercard's guides refer to it for full details, but its specification is not public.
ste: The Mastercard rules for merchants that accept payments from agents. The full text is not public.

plain: A Mastercard service, announced on 2026-06-10, for high-frequency, low-value payments by agents and machines, with credentialing, permissioning, transacting and settlement across cards, accounts and stablecoins. Mastercard says it builds on x402 and opened Early Access with buyer- and seller-side APIs, a toolkit and a sandbox on 2026-10-20; no pricing is published.
ste: A Mastercard service for many small payments by agents and machines. It can settle on cards, accounts or stablecoins.

plain: The name Mastercard gave on 2026-09-30 to five capabilities of Agent Pay: identity, intent, controls, trusted execution and intelligence. Its white paper Trust for agentic commerce (September 2026) also introduces the Agent Pay Ready mark and lists named offerings such as Agentic Disputes; it gives no technical specification, pricing or liability rule.
ste: The name for the five trust parts of Agent Pay: identity, intent, controls, trusted execution and intelligence.

plain: A Mastercard token for web guest checkouts that comes with an expiry date and a one-time DTVC, so an agent can type all three into a normal card form.
ste: A Mastercard token that an agent can put in a usual card form. It comes with a code for one use.

plain: A Mastercard API that registers an agent-captured purchase intent and returns an intentId with tokenized credentials, which the merchant validates at checkout. Field names are published; the schema is not.
ste: A Mastercard API that keeps the purchase intent of the consumer. It gives an intent identifier and a token.

plain: A Mastercard-generated merchant identifier used in Intent API orders; merchants reject a checkout when it does not match their own.
ste: An identifier that Mastercard gives to a merchant. The merchant compares it with the identifier in the intent.

plain: A one-time cryptogram for remote token payments. Mastercard says the Level 3 Agent Pay payload contains a DSRP cryptogram and card metadata.
ste: A cryptographic value for one remote payment with a token.

plain: A Mastercard-issued JWT identifying the consumer, carried in the Level 2 Agent User Identity object; compatible with OpenID Connect ID Tokens.
ste: A token from Mastercard that identifies the consumer. The agent sends it in the request body.

plain: The network-maintained list of agents that passed Mastercard's security review and certification; merchants rely on it through signature verification.
ste: The list of agents that passed the Mastercard examination.

plain: A Mastercard signal, rolling out for US testing (announced 2026-09-30), that estimates how likely it is that an AI agent initiated a transaction. Fields and thresholds are not published.
ste: A Mastercard value that shows how probable it is that an agent started a payment.

plain: The Verifiable Intent mode in which the user signs final checkout and payment values in L2 and no L3 is created.
ste: The mode where the user signs the final values. The agent does not sign credentials.

plain: The Verifiable Intent mode in which the user signs open mandates with constraints and the agent key, and the agent later signs L3a and L3b.
ste: The mode where the user signs limits and the agent signs the final credentials later.

plain: An attack in which the checkout and payment mandates of one Verifiable Intent pair bind different agent keys; prevented by requiring an identical cnf.jwk in both.
ste: An attack where two mandates in one pair have different agent keys.

plain: An L2 and L3 claim in Verifiable Intent that lists references to the mandate disclosures, so a verifier can see that mandates exist even when it cannot read them.
ste: A claim that shows which mandates are in the credential.
